title: Slack desktop workspace data
whyItMatters: Slack keeps a local copy of every signed-in workspace: message cache, files, drafts and the session itself. It shows which companies the person worked with.
source: Slack Help, update the Slack desktop app: the Linux package stores its data in ~/.config/Slack: https://slack.com/intl/en-gb/help/articles/360048367814-Update-the-Slack-desktop-app
notes: Holds the Chromium profile, IndexedDB caches and downloaded files per workspace. The snap keeps its data under ~/snap/slack/<revision>/.config/Slack and the Flatpak under ~/.var/app/com.slack.Slack/config/Slack.

cleanup.signOut: In Slack, click your workspace name in the sidebar and choose Sign out, or sign out all other sessions from your Slack account settings.
steps: Quit Slack from its tray icon.
Uninstall Slack from the App Center if you are removing the app itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes the message cache, downloaded files and drafts for every workspace on this computer. Workspace data on the servers is untouched.
cleanup.source: Slack Help, Sign out of Slack: https://slack.com/help/articles/214613347-Sign-out-of-Slack
